To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a family of activity restructuring operations that can be used to methodically restructure ongoing activities to reduce or avoid performance loss in anticipation of uncertainty, and that we have defined a notion of validity of the activity restructuring operations to guarantee correctness.

activity-split and activity join operations can be applied to complex workflow activities to restructure them and the correctness of the resulting activity is ensured if and only if the original activity is valid.
we have developed a methodical approach to restructuring complex workflow activities and have demonstrated its applicability to real-world workflow management systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a set of activity-split/join operations and their validation to allow users to anticipate and mitigate the impact of uncertainty in workflow activities.
the development of methods to support the methodical restructuring of complex activities in the presence of uncertainty.
the following questions: 1) What are the activity-split and activity join operations for complex workflow activities?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the set of activity restructuring operations is useful in methodically restructuring ongoing activities in anticipation for the uncertainty of the future.

the proposed activity-split and activity join operations provide users the ability to restructure ongoing complex workflow activities in a systematic way to cope with the uncertainty of resource unavailability and delay.
activity-split and activity join are legal if and only if the resulting activities can be performed by the resources available at the time of restructuring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed the theory and methodology of methodically restructuring ongoing activities in complex workflows.

we have proposed a family of activity-join and activity-split operations to support methodical restructuring of ongoing activities and provided the correctness criteria for activity-join and -split operations.
we present a formal model for the activity-join and activity-split operations and define the conditions of their validity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
activity-split and activityjoin operations are a useful tool to restructure ongoing workflow activities to adapt to the changes of resource availabilities and delays.
the notion of validity provides a principled way to guide users in restructuring ongoing activities and to ensure the correctness of new generated activities.
it is possible to restructure ongoing complex workflow activities in a systematic manner without violating the consistency of the workflow execution.
